units.source_text: 我望了望窗外阴沉沉的春天的天空，

en.t: I looked out the window at the gloomy spring sky,

units.source_text: 看了看父亲罩在国民服胸前的袈裟，

en.t: then looked at the priestly robe my father wore over the chest of his national uniform,

units.source_text: 还看了看红光满面的年轻下士们挺起的胸膛，

en.t: and also at the thrust-out chests of the young noncommissioned officers with their ruddy faces,

units.source_text: 好像把金扣子顶得都快蹦起来了。

en.t: as if their gold buttons were being pushed up and were about to pop off.

units.source_text: 我觉得自己仿佛就在他们中间。

en.t: I felt as though I myself were among them.

units.source_text: 不久，我成年后也会被征入伍的。

en.t: Before long, once I came of age, I too would be drafted into the army.

units.source_text: 但即使我当了兵，是不是能像眼前的下士那样忠实地为完成任务而生活呢？

en.t: But even if I became a soldier, would I be able to live as faithfully for the fulfillment of my duty as the noncommissioned officers before me?
At any rate, I stood with one foot in each of two worlds.

units.source_text: 我感到，我还这样年轻，在丑陋的顽固的凸额之下，父亲掌管的死的世界，同年轻人的生的世界是以战争作为媒介而联结在一起的。

en.t: I felt that, young as I still was, beneath my ugly, stubborn protruding forehead, the world of death governed by my father and the world of life belonging to the young were joined together through the medium of war.

units.source_text: 我大概会成为它们的联结点吧。

en.t: I would probably become the point where they were joined.

units.source_text: 假如我战死了，不论眼前这条岔道的哪一边都很清楚，结局是一样的。

en.t: If I died in battle, then whichever side of the fork before me was clear, the ending would be the same.
